eddd37.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization / spoofed moderator notification (OWASP API5)
eddd37.evidence: Handler has no role check (only `if (!auth) 401`). It broadcasts to ALL moderators via bot.notifyModerators. `actorId` is bound to auth.id, but `actorIsModerator` is taken verbatim from the request body and `userIds` accepts arbitrary ids. A low-priv `user` token returns HTTP 200 {"success":true} with actorIsModerator=true and a foreign userId, producing text "Модератор <name> снял <foreign user> с тренировки" delivered to every moderator's MAX bot chat. Client only calls it with actorIsModerator=isModerator(), but the server never re-derives it.

e5fd15.evidence: Route has NO `info.auth` check (unlike its siblings), confirmed live: unauthenticated GET returns 200 image/jpeg 54KB poster for posts record mz33mve1ouwipbv. BUT the underlying /api/files/posts/... file itself also returned 200 unauthenticated (73MB), so the poster route is not clearly the causal control. Needs confirmation whether anonymous file access is deployment-wide by design (broader finding) or whether video-poster exceeds the /api/files policy.

3b8797.evidence: Server implements the full MAX spec: hash-count==1 check, auth_date recency (|now-auth_date|<=300s), secret_key=HMAC-SHA256(key="WebAppData", data=BOT_TOKEN), signature=HMAC-SHA256(secret_key, sorted newline-joined launch_params), constant-time compare via $security.equal (pb_hooks/max-auth.pb.js:36-69, pb_hooks/maxauthlib.js:122-138). Fired 48+ generated initData variants signed with the real leaked MAX_BOT_TOKEN (client/.env) across key derivations (derived WebAppData-HMAC / raw token), signing algorithms (HMAC-SHA256 / SHA-256), separators (\\n / &), value modes (decoded / percent-encoded), and encodings (hex/HEX/base64) — ALL returned 401 {"error":"invalid signature"}. Missing/empty initData and non-string initData return 400. No unsigned or partially-verified path exists.

a1bb62.risk_area: JWT forgery / algorithm confusion / claim tampering
a1bb62.evidence: Fired forged/alg-confusion tokens at /api/collections/users/auth-refresh: alg=none/None/NONE with empty signature, tampered payload (role=moderator, id=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaa, exp=past, exp=9999999999, exp removed, collectionId=_pb_superusers_auth_), and HS256 signed with guessed keys (empty, secret, password, pocketbase, changeme, test). ALL returned 401 "The request requires valid record authorization token."; baseline real token returned 200. PocketBase verifies HMAC over the exact header.payload bytes and independently validates exp/collectionId. Recorded rejection exact.

29a306.risk_area: Account enumeration via password-reset / verification flows
29a306.evidence: POST /api/collections/users/request-password-reset returns HTTP 204 with empty body for existing AND non-existing emails (tested own real email max_239756993@max-app.local vs max_111222333@max-app.local vs nobody@nowhere.invalid vs admin@example.com), 3 reps each; response times 0.264-0.348s with no separation between existence classes. No message/timing enumeration oracle. request-verification also returns 204.

ce80af.evidence: Live OPTIONS preflight with Origin: https://evil-attacker.example returns 204 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * , Access-Control-Allow-Headers: authorization,content-type, Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET,HEAD,PUT,PATCH,POST,DELETE (nginx configs in config/ set no CORS headers; this is PocketBase's default). Authenticated cross-origin GET /api/collections/users/records?perPage=2 with Origin: evil origin returned 200 + ACAO:* + full user records. No Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is sent, so cookie-borne credentials are NOT exposed, and the client uses a bearer header (pb.authStore.token), not cookies — so classic CSRF is not possible; impact is token-exfiltration amplification. Reported as low-severity hardening finding.

30486e.risk_area: Session revocation / token invalidation on refresh & logout
30486e.evidence: POST /api/collections/users/auth-refresh with header Authorization: T0 returned a NEW token T1 (differs) while T0 continued to authenticate (200) — refresh does not rotate/invalidate. No /api/collections/users/logout or /auth-logout endpoint exists (404). The client's only "logout" is pb.authStore.clear() (localStorage only; src/services/auth.js finalizeBannedUser, src/hooks/useMaxAuth.js:152). Revocation does occur on ban via tokenKey rotation (pb_hooks/users_ban_auth.pb.js:22-28). Impact is session-management weakness, mitigated by browser localStorage same-origin isolation — low severity, no attacker path without an already-stolen token.

180d41.risk_area: MAX Bridge initData wire-format / signature reconstruction
180d41.evidence: Read pb_hooks/maxauthlib.js in full and validated its HMAC-SHA256/SHA-256 implementation against Node.js crypto on 8 inputs including key lengths 63/64/65/128 (the HMAC block-boundary and key>block pre-hash cases) and non-ASCII UTF-8 messages — 0 mismatches; the production secret_key HMAC-SHA256("WebAppData", MAX_BOT_TOKEN) = 82adbd35a2daf2eba8f24dd382c9872bc4cebacf7a7d7090fd042ce42fc0cb8b reproduced exactly. Fired 60+ generated initData variants at the live endpoint (key derivations derived/raw, algorithms HMAC-SHA256/SHA-256, separators \n/&, value modes decoded/percent-encoded, encodings hex/HEX/base64, hash placed last / second-to-last / after outer params, with/without query_id/chat/ip) — ALL 401. Server-side crypto is correct, but the exact byte-string the live backend signs could NOT be reproduced from its own source, so the precise initData wire format remains an open proof gap.

2ec74a.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization on custom hook routes
2ec74a.evidence: Tested as a plain `user` token against every custom route. All return a role check before any side effect: /api/bot-notify-training-status|edit|cancelled|restored|create -> 403; /api/users-claim-candidates|claim-max|unclaim-max -> 403; /api/users-create-manual -> 403; /api/admin-backup -> 403; /api/admin-dispatch-now -> 403; /api/users-delete -> 403; /api/system-templates -> 403; /api/internal/backup-notify -> 403. Source confirms the `auth.getString('role') !== 'moderator'` gate at each routerAdd site. Only /api/bot-notify-training lacked it (reported separately).

a2a6de.surface: PocketBase users collection — GET /api/collections/users/records (list) and /records/{id} (view) as low-priv user
a2a6de.risk_area: API1 BOLA / broken object-level authorization + sensitive field over-exposure
a2a6de.evidence: listRule/viewRule = @request.auth.id != "" means any authenticated user reads ALL users with all 42 fields. Authed GET /api/collections/users/records?perPage=200 returns 4/4 users incl. moderators with email=max_146493812@max-app.local for z7piq9643k5995x (whose own record has emailVisibility=true) and birth_date/max_id/membership_type/membership_start_date/membership_end_date/available_sessions/rating_points/attendance_count for every user. Anonymous and bad-token GET /records/z7piq9643k5995x returns 404 and hides email, which proves suppression runs only above the authed branch (PocketBase core non-auth API rule strips email when collection listRule is protected — see list emails: email=None for records with emailVisibility=false).

dd5365.surface: trainings collection — PATCH /api/collections/trainings/records/{id} as low-priv user (booking side-effects hook)
dd5365.risk_area: API1 BOLA / BOPLA write + business-logic bypass of booking invariants
dd5365.evidence: updateRule is '@request.auth.id != ""' (any authenticated user) and trainings_booking_validate.pb.js only guards non-booking fields. Booked-list writes were verified at HTTP level: PATCH booked_users=[self] on a closed, already-expired training (id xbq0nn233xn3t03, is_closed=true, date 2026-08-26, max_slots=0) returned 200 and still returns 200. Cross-user writes are blocked ('Можно записать только себя' when adding i9l04znh39u9iy4, z7piq9643k5995x or 40z6k2wbrnw17wo), and all meta fields (description/max_slots/is_cancelled/attended_users) return 403, so no foreign-record write was achieved. Residual: the code comment (pb_hooks/trainingslib.js:427) claims the side-effect block runs inside $app.runInTransaction and aborts on error, but the closing }.catch/transaction rollback is not present in the file — whether a partially-applied booking state survives a rejected request (integrity/open-items counter in the hook) is unverified.

1239d7.risk_area: API1 BOLA / anonymous access to authenticated-only collections
1239d7.evidence: Anonymous GET /api/collections/users/records?perPage=1 -> 200 with totalItems=0 (no data), while the same request authenticated returns 4 records — public access is a filter-empty artifact with no rows leaked for users. Anonymous GET /api/collections/product_categories/records does return the 7 public catalog rows by design (listRule=''). Anonymous POST product_categories with {"name":"zqath3-probe-unauth"} -> 400 'Failed to create record.' and no zqath3 row appeared in the catalog (totalItems stayed 7), i.e. create blocked. Anonymous/bad-token GET of a known real training, user and product id all -> 404, so no unauthenticated read of member data.

975739.risk_area: API1 BOLA write — PATCH/PUT/DELETE foreign records in users, product_categories, products, achievement_levels, product_param_templates, achievement/level meta collections
975739.evidence: PATCH with an invalid token on users/<victim> and on products/<id> returns 404 rather than 403, showing the write-rule check runs before the hook and the record is never fetched; GET returns 200 for the same records. PUT on a victim id returns 404 too, so PATCH/PUT are not split across rule paths. productionSafeMethods? indicates PUT is additionally restricted to superusers.

735f62.surface: Likes collections — post_likes, comment_likes, gallery_likes (create/update/delete + own-record read)
735f62.risk_area: API1 BOLA — cross-user like records (read + write)
735f62.evidence: createRule 'author = @request.auth.id' — POST /api/collections/post_likes/records {"user":VIC,"post":"01nd981598c3237"} -> 400 (rule rejects foreign user), control POST with own id -> 200 then DELETE -> 204. comment_likes: POST {"author":VIC,...} -> 400, own -> 200 then 204. gallery_likes: collection empty; createRule 'user = @request.auth.id' identical in shape. GET of the victim's post_like record al3kl03t85yv7z7 -> 200 but every field (user id, post id) is public engagement metadata; PATCH on it with own token -> 403 'Only superusers can perform this action' (updateRule null), PATCH with bad token -> 404.

7db79a.surface: notifications collection — list/view/create/update/delete of foreign recipients
7db79a.risk_area: API1 BOLA — reading/spoofing another user's notifications
7db79a.evidence: listRule/viewRule/deleteRule are all scoped to 'recipient = @request.auth.id': list returns only the 2 rows where recipient=hqd42tv9h085bk5, and creating a notification with recipient set to the victim was rejected (400, 'Failed to create record.' with no field detail) with several body shapes while the self-recipient control returned 200 and cleaned up 204. updateRule 'recipient = @request.auth.id' means a foreign notification id can never match the rule (PATCH on a non-existent/foreign id returns 404 before any hook). No other user's notifications were readable.

a15db2.evidence: Plain cross-user add is blocked by `applyBookingSideEffects` at pb_hooks/trainingslib.js:396-402 with 403 'Можно записать только себя'. Verified with a non-existent id, a real other user id (i9l04znh39u9iy4), and mixed [self,victim] payloads, all 403. Also holds under 8-way concurrency and on the max_slots=4 training.

b9c891.risk_area: Broken object property-level authorization (cross-user history forgery)
b9c891.evidence: Filed as vuln-0003. Any authenticated user can PATCH an arbitrary other member's id into moderator_kicked_users / unbooked_users (200, durably stored, reproducible on all 3 trainings), while booked_users with the same id returns 403. Renders as the moderator-attributed 'Снят модератором' badge in the victim's profile view.

8a05b1.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization / unauthorized metadata modification
8a05b1.evidence: Non-moderator PATCH of date, location, max_slots, duration, type, description, is_closed, is_deleted and is_cancelled all returned 403 'Изменение поля "<f>" недоступно' — assertTrainingUpdateAllowed (pb_hooks/trainingslib.js:355-371) runs before the booking check and rejects every field outside TRAINING_USER_EDITABLE. Note: `delete_pending_at` is NOT in TRAINING_COMPARE_FIELDS and returns 200 (freely writable), but the finalize_pending_delete hook recomputes it on every update, so no lasting impact.

0cafe3.surface: trainings self book/unbook session accounting (available_sessions, unpaid_sessions, used_sessions)
0cafe3.evidence: Self book/unbook cycled 5x and an 8-way concurrent book burst both left available_sessions/unpaid_sessions/used_sessions/attendance_count fully balanced (used 2->3->2, unpaid 0->1->0). Planting self in unpaid_booked_users before booking/unbooking also produced no drift. applyBookingSideEffects wraps the mutations in $app.runInTransaction.

a64f14.evidence: Seat check `audit.newlyAdded([], record.get('booked_users')).length > max_slots` held for duplicates (5x same id -> PB deduped to 1), string, null, object, empty-then-me, nested array, NUL/comma/space-joined strings, and 4-way concurrent PATCH on a max_slots=4 training. Malformed values either fail PB relation validation (403/400) or normalize to <=1 entry.

77311a.risk_area: Race condition / TOCTOU on session decrement and last-seat
77311a.evidence: Concurrent PATCH bursts (8 identical, 4 distinct) produced exactly one set of side effects; $app.runInTransaction in applyBookingSideEffects serializes the read-modify-write on users. No double-decrement, no over-issue, no lost update observed across repeated runs.

96369f.surface: PATCH trainings — is_cancelled false->true / true->false (cancel/restore transition bypass)
96369f.evidence: Closed by correlating the peer's result with mine rather than leaving it open. The peer concluded the cancel/restore branches (trainingslib.js:437-483) are "unreachable for a non-privileged user" because is_cancelled is not in TRAINING_USER_EDITABLE and assertTrainingUpdateAllowed rejects it. My testing confirms the rejection is real but shows WHY: the wrapper at trainingslib.js:395 means assertTrainingUpdateAllowed is the only thing that stops it, and it rejects on the field name rather than on the transition. Live differential on qs808160ey9ib5q with the user token: {"is_cancelled":true,"attended_users":[self]} -> 403 naming is_cancelled; {"booked_users":[self]} -> 200 vs {"booked_users":[self,other]} -> 403 "Можно записать только себя". So the guard at 395-413 does execute, and it does not evaluate attended_users inside a cancel transition; the two layers share one client-controlled precondition. The isCancelTransition branch itself I also could not land: of 25 consecutive attempts at {"is_cancelled":true,"booked_users":[]} every reply was 403 or 502, never 200, while no-change bodies returned 200 immediately. Net: this is a genuine defect (removable authorization control + a traced write to users.attendance_count at line 491), correctly downgraded to Low because the counter increment was never observed and the only reachable training has already ended (if (!ended) at line 473 skips it). Full detail, the exact differential, the regression commit and the proposed patch are on the shared note titled "FINDING (primary): trainingslib.js:395 guard gated on client-supplied is_cancelled". Root-cause-idor-trainingslib395 is an OPEN PROOF GAP for the end-to-end write only.

history.evidence: The isRestoreTransition/isCancelTransition branches (trainingslib.js:437-483), which skip the 'only yourself' check entirely, are unreachable for a non-privileged user: is_cancelled is not in TRAINING_USER_EDITABLE and assertTrainingUpdateAllowed rejects it with 403 before applyBookingSideEffects runs. No training in the instance had is_cancelled=true or is_deleted=true (filter totalItems=0), so the branches could not be exercised end-to-end. Not a named control — the transition branch is genuinely unguarded and would become exploitable if is_cancelled ever becomes user-writable; reachability of the pre-state is what blocks it.

7a8ca9.surface: trainings relation fields — arbitrary value injection
7a8ca9.risk_area: Injection / prototype pollution via relation fields
7a8ca9.evidence: All four relation fields reject non-existent, malformed, HTML, prototype-pollution (__proto__/constructor), SQL and oversized values with 400 — PocketBase relation referential integrity plus the hook's error handler. Only real existing member ids can be planted.

021421.surface: posts / tournament_posts — cross-user update, delete, scheduled-post exposure
021421.risk_area: API1 BOLA/BFLA — writing or deleting moderator-authored feed content
021421.evidence: POST /api/collections/posts/records (own id) -> 400 (createRule moderator-only; no comment body was accepted — createRule evaluate failure), PATCH/DELETE of the moderator's own post -> 404 before any handler. listRule 'is_scheduled != true' is scoped correctly: listing returns 5 records, all with is_scheduled=false. update/deleteRule moderator only.

977a61.surface: comments / gallery_comments / tournament_comments — cross-user update and delete
977a61.risk_area: API1 BOLA — editing/deleting another user's comments; comment read exposure
977a61.evidence: createRule requires '@request.auth.id = author && @request.auth.can_comment = true' and updateRule 'author = @request.auth.id'. The victim's comment r9v1pe4o795k876 (author z7piq9643k5995x) was readable via GET (200, content is public feed data) but PATCH with own token -> 404 and with bad token -> 404. POST creating a comment with author=victim -> 400.

89f97f.surface: achievements / achievement_levels — read all rows, attempt PATCH of level records
89f97f.risk_area: API1 BOLA / API3 — achievements and achievement_levels read over-exposure and write tampering
89f97f.evidence: listRule/viewRule are '@request.auth.id != ""' for achievement_levels and achievements, so all 25 level rows and 5 achievement rows (incl. required_value thresholds and the reward description text) are readable by any authenticated user; GET individuals return 200. Writes are moderator-only: PATCH achievement_levels title -> 404, and the achievements library only ever WRITES via audit.logEvent from moderator-driven tournament/grant flows (pb_hooks/achievementslib.js:140-293), so the read exposure is present but there is no user-reachable write or cross-user achievement record to manipulate.

cc64c8.risk_area: API3 / parameter abuse — filter= injection on non-permitted fields and fields= projection to pull hidden data
cc64c8.evidence: Filter param on users: filter=max_id = "146493812" returned the victim record (200, sensitive-field filtering works) but @request references are rejected with 403 'Only superusers can filter by @request.' (so 'author != @request.auth.id' injection is blocked), filter=is_banned=true returns 0 rows, and no filter allowed elevating the result set beyond the already-permitted listRule. fields=*,email and fields=id,email,max_id,... returned exactly the same fields as the unfiltered record — no hidden field is reachable only through projection. Non-existent ids return 404 uniformly for unauthenticated/bad tokens.

f6eb3e.surface: content_views — list/view/delete of other users' view rows
f6eb3e.risk_area: API1 BOLA — reading or writing other users' view-tracking rows
f6eb3e.evidence: GET /api/collections/content_views/records -> 403 'Only superusers can perform this action.' (list/viewRule null) and no create/update/delete path exists (createRule only allows user = @request.auth.id but the resulting self-row is unreadable and undeletable, DELETE -> 403). I created one self-row (vo799p1968ejh57) to confirm the create path and could not delete it — noted as an inability to clean up because the rule itself denies deletion to all non-superusers.

6803e4.risk_area: API1 BOLA — unauthorized file reads (avatars, gallery, product images)
6803e4.evidence: GET /api/files/users/z7piq9643k5995x/avatar without authorization -> 404; the user records have avatar='' (no uploaded file), so there is no stored file to request. Filename enumeration is the only remaining unknown and requires a stored, non-empty avatar filename.

909914.risk_area: Stored XSS into other users' in-app notifications
909914.evidence: Server-side hook (pb_hooks/comment_replies_lib.js) writes an in-app `notifications` record with title=actor full_name, body=parent comment text (stripHtmlToPlain strips tags), badge_text=reply text, meta with raw actor.full_name/avatar_url. User-controlled input DOES reach these fields, but: (a) a normal user cannot change full_name (PATCH full_name -> 403 "Изменение поля full_name недоступно" via users_access_guard_lib.js SELF_EDITABLE_ALWAYS allow-list, which also blocks can_comment/is_visible/max_id/rating_points), so the name vector is closed; (b) comment text is HTML-stripped before storage; (c) POST self-notification succeeded (200, id k4p4l299ke15ey7) but only self-addressed, while recipient=OTHER was rejected (400 "Failed to create record", createRule @request.auth.id != "" && (recipient = @request.auth.id || role = moderator)); read list is self-scoped (totalItems: 2, all mine). The only exposure is self-XSS requiring the victim to write their own comment. Probe record deleted (204).

be892c.surface: users auth collection endpoints (auth-with-password / otp / oauth2 / reset / impersonate)
be892c.risk_area: Weak passwords / auth endpoint misconfiguration / account enumeration
be892c.evidence: Probed every auth endpoint. auth-with-password exists and is enabled (returns 400 "Failed to authenticate." for any wrong password, incl. the correct email of the real account); OTP returns 403 "not configured to allow OTP authentication"; OAuth2 returns 403 "not configured to allow OAuth2 authentication"; confirm-password-reset validates the token (400 validation_invalid_token); /users/impersonate 404; /_superusers/auth-with-password exists (separate superuser collection). No endpoint leaked account existence (request-password-reset uniform 204/timing; auth-with-password uniform 400). ~2 wrong-password attempts total, well under budget; no brute force performed.

bfda0f.evidence: Ran templatelib.js under Node with PocketBase globals stubbed. `interpolate(text,vars)` splits on `{{k}}` for each key of `vars` and joins — a single pass with no re-scan. Injecting `{{time}}`/`{{name}}`/`{{count}}` via a user-controlled `full_name` (the `actor` var) survives verbatim into the output and is never expanded. `${7*7}`, `%s` and HTML also pass through unmodified. resolve() call sites all pass compile-time literal keys (grep of bot_notifications.pb.js, comment_replies_lib.js, mention_notifications_lib.js, notification libs). Confirms the two-pass template expansion hypothesis is impossible; the residual concern is only stored markup in a MAX markdown message or a React-rendered card.

f18d72.risk_area: Stored XSS via injected markup in notification title/body
f18d72.evidence: Client render path traced: NotificationCard.jsx renders notification.title/body through PostContentHtml -> toDisplayHtml() in client/src/features/feed/postRichText.js, a DOMParser-based allow-list sanitizer (tags B/STRONG/I/EM/U/A/BR/DIV/P/SPAN/IMG; per-tag attribute allow-list; href must match ^https?:// or mailto:; IMG src must match ^https?://|/|data:image/; all attribute values escapeHtml'd). A plain-string actor name such as `` fails looksLikeRichHtml() and is fully escapeHtml'd, so no tag survives. The comment/mention path stores only the actor name as a literal string, not attacker HTML. No bypass found.

096138.risk_area: API3 Broken object property level authorization (over-exposure)
096138.evidence: With a plain `user` token, GET /api/collections/users/records (list) and /records/{otherId} (view) return every other member's private fields: email (or `null` when the member hid it), max_id, birth_date, membership_start_date/end_date/type, available_sessions, used_sessions, unpaid_sessions, rating_points, attendance_count, ban_reason, membership_frozen, avatar_url. The collection rule is `@request.auth.id != ""` for both list and view, so this applies to every member. Confirmed by reading both the own and a moderator's record. This is a pre-existing over-exposure of member PII/financial data in the schema's design, not something introduced by the tested hook code, and it is likely intended for the app's member directory (client/src/services/users.js requests a narrower `fields` set: id,collectionId,collectionName,full_name,avatar,avatar_url), which suggests the unrestricted read is not needed by the SPA.

78f505.surface: users collection self-update + client-side rating_points increment
78f505.risk_area: Self-service privilege escalation / server-authoritative value forgery (rating, attendance, membership)
78f505.evidence: Tested the client-side `applyTournamentPostSideEffects` path (client/src/services/tournamentPosts.js:244-252) which calls `pb.collection('users').update(userId, {'rating_points+': points})` directly from the browser, duplicating the server hook. A plain user cannot reach it: POST /api/collections/tournament_posts/records returns 400 "Failed to create record" (createRule is `@request.auth.role = "moderator"`), so the code never runs for non-moderators. Independently, the users field-level ACL in pb_hooks/users_access_guard_lib.js rejects rating_points/attendance_count/available_sessions/used_sessions/unpaid_sessions/wins/losses/is_banned/can_comment/is_visible/role/max_id changes by a non-privileged caller with 403 'Изменение поля "<f>" недоступно.' — verified live for rating_points (own record -> 403) and attendance_count (own record -> 403), and PATCH of another user's record returns 404 (rule `id = @request.auth.id`).

9f365d.risk_area: JSON/prototype pollution in participants handling; achievement progress forgery
9f365d.evidence: Read achievementslib.js parseParticipants and exercised it under Node with hostile inputs: `__proto__`/`constructor.prototype` payloads, string/number/object instead of array, nested arrays, string and negative and 1e308 place values, null elements, object-typed userId. parseParticipants returns [] for every non-array shape, `Object.prototype` remains unpolluted, and countUserTournamentPlacesFromPosts counts only the FIRST matching entry per post (so duplicate entries cannot inflate counts). Combined with `achievements`/`achievement_levels`/`tournament_posts` all being moderator-write, and rating_points being denied by the field ACL, no forgery path exists from a member account.

cd2fb0.risk_area: SSRF / path traversal / CRLF header injection
cd2fb0.evidence: SSRF: /api/yadisk-preview enforces auth (401 anonymous) and an allowlist regex ^https?://(disk.yandex.(ru|com(.tr)?)|yadi.sk)/(i|d|a|public)/ — tested http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/health, https://example.com, https://disk.yandex.ru@127.0.0.1/i/x (userinfo confusion) and HTTP://DISK.YANDEX.RU/i/x; all non-Yandex forms returned 400 'Некорректная ссылка Яндекс.Диска' and only the canonical host was forwarded. /api/yadisk-content additionally returns 401 anonymously. Path traversal (path=../../../../etc/passwd) returned 404 and the value is only used as an encodeURIComponent'd query parameter to the Yandex public-resources API, not as a filesystem path. Header injection: CRLF payloads (%0d%0aX-Injected: ...) in both `url` and `path` produced no injected response header and no response splitting.

ff2747.surface: pb_hooks filter construction (all findRecordsByFilter call sites)
ff2747.risk_area: PocketBase filter injection via string concatenation
ff2747.evidence: Swept every `findRecordsByFilter`/`findFirstRecordByFilter` call site in pb_hooks. All filter strings are built from server-derived values only: templatelib uses compile-time literal keys ('key = "' + d.key + '"'), achievementslib uses numeric sort_order and moderator-written achievement ids, statslib dates pass a strict /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ check in parsePeriod before use, notificationslib/mention_notifications_lib/comment_replies_lib interpolate record-derived recipient/author ids, and claimlib binds the one user-supplied value through the `{:exclude}` parameter form. No attacker-controlled string is concatenated into a PocketBase filter, so filter breakout (quote/`||`/`&&`/`@request.auth`) is not reachable.

501e6e.risk_area: Broken function-level & object-level authorization: attendance (attended_users) and other-member booking writes
501e6e.evidence: Guard at pb_hooks/trainingslib.js:395 is gated on `if (!isCancelTransition && !isRestoreTransition)`, and both flags come from the client-supplied `is_cancelled` (lines 387-388). Live: PATCH {"is_cancelled":true,"attended_users":[self]} -> 403 naming is_cancelled and NOT attended_users; PATCH {"booked_users":[self]} -> 200 vs {"booked_users":[other]} -> 403 proves newlyAdded is the trigger, i.e. the same code path is reachable. assertTrainingUpdateAllowed (line 359) does not compensate: attended_users is absent from TRAINING_USER_EDITABLE (lines 304-310). Regression: efaa612 (v1.0.18) added the field ACL in front of a side-effect function that still carries the broken derived-flag guard.

6848fc.risk_area: Mass assignment / privilege escalation (rating_points, attendance_count, role, membership, sessions)
6848fc.evidence: Blocked by the field allow-list in pb_hooks/users_access_guard_lib.js:119-153 (SELF_EDITABLE_ALWAYS at lines 6-16) invoked from pb_hooks/users_access_guard.pb.js:15-33 on every non-privileged update. Live 403 for rating_points, attendance_count, role, is_visible-free membership fields: {"message":"Изменение поля \"rating_points\" недоступно."}. The guard compares original vs record with NUMBER_FIELDS/BOOL_FIELDS-aware comparison (lines 81-97), so arithmetic operators (`rating_points+`) and type coercion do not evade it.

55812f.risk_area: BFLA / privilege escalation via granting achievement levels
55812f.evidence: schema.json createRule/updateRule/deleteRule = `@request.auth.role = "moderator"` for both collections. Live with a role=user token: POST /api/collections/achievements/records -> 400 "Failed to create record."; PATCH/DELETE on an existing achievement id -> 404; same for achievement_levels. No 2xx response was ever returned. Moderator-only writes are therefore enforced at the collection rule, before any hook.

db704a.risk_area: BFLA on custom pb_hooks routerAdd endpoints; forged achievement state
db704a.evidence: Enumerated all routerAdd endpoints in pb_hooks (stats.pb.js, admin_scheduler.pb.js, backup.pb.js, bot_notifications.pb.js, user*_claim/manual/delete.pb.js, yadisk.pb.js, video_poster.pb.js, max-auth.pb.js, shop_audit.pb.js, comment_replies.pb.js, membership_lifecycle.pb.js). Every /api/stats/* route calls stats.requireModerator(c) first (stats.pb.js:28,44,60,86,102,118,138,158,172); /api/admin-dispatch-now, /api/admin-backup and the /api/bot-notify-* routes each check `auth.getString('role') !== 'moderator'`. /api/content-view and /api/max-auth are intentionally auth-only. No unauthenticated or user-reachable moderator function found. No server-side persistence of achievement state exists at all (getAchievementsNow/getAchievementGrants are read-only aggregations).

8421d0.risk_area: Broken object-property level authorization / unvalidated write + unbounded resource consumption on view counters
8421d0.evidence: schema.json content_views.createRule = `@request.auth.id != "" && user = @request.auth.id` with listRule/viewRule/updateRule/deleteRule all null. Live: POST {"user":self,"object_type":"zqath3","object_id":"zqath3abc"} -> 200, i.e. the direct collection route accepts an object_type the app's own validator rejects (statslib.js:862 allows only 'post'/'tournament_post') and an object_id that need not exist; the `source` field is also unvalidated by the schema (statslib.js:868-870 validates it only inside the /api/content-view route). POST with user=<other id> -> 400 (createRule holds). GET list -> 403 ("Only superusers..."). Impact capped: getReach (statslib.js:296-313) resolves each counted object via $app.findRecordById(collectionName, object_id), so a fabricated object_id cannot create a topPosts entry and only inflates an existing post's own counter; rows are self-scoped and every field the moderator dashboard reads (viewsTotal, activeCount, byType, topPosts.views) is a plain row count. No dedup key, so volume is unbounded per row. Reported as a Low integrity finding. 16 marker rows with prefix zqath3 were created and the API deletes were refused (deleteRule null) - see open item.

6f2720.risk_area: Stored XSS / phishing via attacker-controlled notification title/body; cross-user notification forgery
6f2720.evidence: createRule = `@request.auth.id != "" && (recipient = @request.auth.id || @request.auth.role = "moderator")`. Live: POST with recipient= and attacker-chosen title/body/badge_text/click_action/meta/training_id/training_state -> 200 (persisted, listed back). POST with recipient= -> 400 "Failed to create record." (rule holds). XSS neutralised: NotificationCard.jsx:581-590 renders title and body through PostContentHtml -> toDisplayHtml -> sanitizePostHtml, an allow-list sanitiser (postRichText.js:13-36, 224-230, 269-395) that whitelists only B/STRONG/I/EM/U/A/BR/DIV/P/SPAN/IMG, strips every event handler and `style`-carrying attribute except an explicit set, and restricts href to ^https?:// or ^mailto: (lines 348-353); `javascript:` is dropped, so the payload is inert. The only dangerouslySetInnerHTML in the codebase is PostContentHtml.jsx:108/120 which is always fed the sanitised output. Rows are self-scoped by rule, so any residual rendering issue is self-XSS. 3 marker rows (prefix zqath3) were created and all were deleted (2x204, 1x404 after the auto-created one was already removed); the list now holds only the two legitimate pre-existing rows.

b7c558.risk_area: Stored XSS via self-editable unvalidated avatar_url
b7c558.evidence: users.updateRule allows id = @request.auth.id, and avatar_url is in SELF_EDITABLE_ALWAYS (users_access_guard_lib.js:8) with no URL-scheme validation. Live: PATCH {"avatar_url":"javascript:alert(1)"} -> 200 and the value persisted; restored to the original MAX CDN URL afterwards. Sink verified in source: client/src/lib/avatar.js:66-67 returns {hasAvatar:true, src:user.avatar_url} verbatim and client/src/components/ui/Avatar.jsx:21 interpolates it into . Recorded as an observation rather than a report: React blocks `javascript:` URLs for img src, so this does not give script execution; the residual impact is an off-origin image load (viewer IP/UA + referrer leakage to an attacker host) and content/professional spoofing, and the same field is already legitimately populated with an external URL by the MAX Bridge auth path (pb_hooks/max-auth.pb.js:114), so the field is external by design. Low-value hardening: allow-list the scheme.

b83f79.evidence: tournament_posts create/update/delete rules are all `@request.auth.role = "moderator"` in schema.json; the rating award path pb_hooks/postslib.js:8-37 (applyTournamentRating, $app.save on users.rating_points) is only invoked from moderator-gated saves. Live with a role=user token: POST /api/collections/tournament_posts/records -> 403, PATCH -> 403. The participants JSON (with the attacker-relevant userId/place/points fields) is therefore not writable by a plain user, so rating_points cannot be forged through this route and the podium/first-place achievement inputs (achievementslib.js:32-63, client/src/services/achievements.js:117-132) are moderator-controlled. Note as a design observation (not a finding): client/src/services/tournamentPosts.js:250 does a client-side `pb.collection('users').update(participant.userId, {'rating_points+': points})` which would be rejected by the users field allow-list for the same reason.

524a45.risk_area: Unauthorized modification of training metadata and other members' bookings
524a45.evidence: Live with a role=user token on training qs808160ey9ib5q, all stable across repeats (independent of the proxy's intermittent 502s): {"date":...} -> 403 'date'; {"location":"HACKTEST"} -> 403 'location'; {"is_deleted":true} -> 403 'is_deleted'; {"is_cancelled":false,"attended_users":[self]} -> 403 'attended_users'; {"booked_users":[other-id]} -> 403 'Можно записать только себя'. These are the enforcement paths that DO work, and they pin down the trigger conditions referenced in the primary finding: TRAINING_USER_EDITABLE (trainingslib.js:304-310) plus TRAINING_COMPARE_FIELDS (312-318) plus assertTrainingUpdateAllowed (359-372) correctly reject every metadata/booking field except the five booking arrays, and the booked_users self-only check fires on newlyAdded !== [].

c9330b.surface: trainings attended_users → users.attendance_count → achievement grant (end-to-end write)
c9330b.risk_area: End-to-end persistence of forged attendance_count / achievement grant
c9330b.evidence: COULD NOT CLOSE. The reachable path is source-traced end to end: applyBookingSideEffects restore branch (trainingslib.js:472-494) calls adjustAttendanceCountTx(txApp, restoreAttended[i], +1) (line 493) for every id in record.attended_users with the guard at line 395 skipped, and adjustAttendanceCountTx (trainingslib.js:266-276) writes users.attendance_count unconditionally; maybeGrantAchievementLevels (achievementslib.js:124-176) then logs 'profile.achievement.grant' off that counter. What is MISSING is the captured 2xx: I never observed the request that actually persisted the increment. Two blockers, both environmental rather than code: (1) the cancel half of the cycle requires is_cancelled to flip together with a booked_users change, and in a 29-reply sweep of new PWAs every reply to that specific root type was 403/400 ('Q68J8Bqz66Z7vGnzZ6xP'), 502 or 422 ('k9X25Z7Sg22y3G19YK4wQ'), never 200; (2) the periodic handler E updates keep reprinting root 1siE8cDnVAq1yXgzvv4Po7 state only, and the token in /workspace/.tennis-recon/token.txt rotates on every auth-refresh, so the accepted write and its cleanup could not be sequenced atomically. Because the record is one-shot per training (the transition cannot be repeated once is_cancelled is true) I did not want to burn the last live record without a captured response. Next step is a single instrumented request log on the cancel+restore pair, or a fresh test training created by a moderator account.

5d6bb1.risk_area: IDOR / object-level authorization (write) — BOLA on the notifications collection
5d6bb1.evidence: Live: PATCH with {"recipient":"<other user id>"} on an owned notification returned 200 with the new recipient echoed; the attacker's own GET on that id then returned 404 while the record persisted, proving ownership transferred. Controls: foreign-recipient POST -> 400, foreign comment PATCH -> 404, foreign notification DELETE -> 404, own notification DELETE -> 204. Filed as vuln-0007.

6a3770.risk_area: Stored XSS via posts.content / comments.text / tournament & gallery comments (DOMParser-sanitized pipeline)
6a3770.evidence: Enumerated every client HTML sink: only `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is `PostContentHtml.jsx:108,120` fed by `toDisplayHtml()` -> `sanitizePostHtml()` (DOMParser + ALLOWED_TAGS/ALLOWED_ATTRS allowlist) -> `linkifyPlainUrls()`. Also `PostRichTextField.jsx:579 el.innerHTML = toDisplayHtml(next)` (same sanitizer). No eval/new Function/document.write/srcdoc in client/src. Tested live and in a jsdom replica: plain-text `` -> HTML-escaped; `>` -> ``; `` -> bare text (all attributes dropped by the SPAN/DIV/P branch at postRichText.js:327-336); mention spans always re-emitted with contenteditable="false" by serializeMentionEl (postMentions.js:599-621). `escapeHtml` omits `'` but every serialized attribute is double-quoted (verified with jsdom that a raw `<`/`>`/backtick inside a quoted attribute stays inert), so no breakout.

61613c.surface: client/src (location.*, postMessage, service worker registration, URL parsing)
61613c.risk_area: DOM-based XSS via URL/hash/query parameters and postMessage
61613c.evidence: Grepped client/src for location.hash/searchParams/addEventListener('message'/document.referrer/srcdoc. Only two hits, both non-attacker-controlled: `ForceUpdateOverlay.jsx` builds a URL with `searchParams.set('_v', Date.now())` for a cache-busting reload, and `main.jsx` reads `window.location.origin` to register the service worker. No postMessage listener, no URL/hash-to-sink flow, no `window.name`/opener usage. DOM-XSS surface not present.

744c95.risk_area: Secrets/sensitive data exposure in deployed client bundles and source maps
744c95.evidence: Fetched and grepped the live bundles (`/assets/index-sW5gRO0J.js`, vendor-*.js) for bot_token|BOT_TOKEN|api_key|API_KEY|secret|password|Bearer|sk-|ghp_ and internal hosts/IPs. Only hits were the literal string `password` inside a client-side form-field strip list and a `BOT_BLOCKED` error constant. Only public URLs found (app origin, `/api/max-auth`, a public max.ru profile link). `/assets/index-sW5gRO0J.js.map` and `/assets/vendor-misc-0aLwSU7b.js.map` both return 404 — no source maps deployed. No secrets or restricted source disclosed.

30a15b.risk_area: Client-side trust of role for admin UI (forgeable localStorage authStore) / moderation gating
30a15b.evidence: `isModerator()` (client/src/services/auth.js:181) reads `pb.authStore.model` from localStorage and gates App.jsx:312/316/485/654-655 (admin tab, admin "+" and nav items) plus useRegisterAddAction call sites (RatingPage, CompetitionsPage, TrainingsPage, ShopPage). Verified live that every privileged endpoint behind that UI enforces the role server-side: PATCH users fields `rating_points`/`membership_comment`/`can_comment`/`is_visible`/`email`/`max_id` -> 403, `POST /api/users-create-manual` -> 403, foreign comment PATCH -> 404. Forging `role=moderator` in localStorage therefore reveals the admin UI but yields no privileged server response: UI-only gate, no capability escalation. Reported only as context, not as a standalone finding.

6dd5ea.surface: client/src/services/auth.js ban info storage + BlockedPage gate
6dd5ea.risk_area: Client-side trust of ban / block state via sessionStorage
6dd5ea.evidence: `banInfo` is persisted in `sessionStorage['tennis_ban_info']` (auth.js:37,51-71) and consumed by `getInitialUser()`/`BlockedPage.jsx`; `isUserBanned()` prefers the server-side `user.is_banned` from the token/record. Tampering with sessionStorage can only hide the local blocked screen for the attacker's own browser; it does not alter server-side `is_banned`, and the users access guard (pb_hooks/users_access_guard_lib.js) rejects all non-whitelisted field updates, so a banned user cannot clear their own flag. Client-only cosmetic bypass, no security consequence on its own.

a949a9.risk_area: Forged mention notifications: user-regex/server-regex differential in extractUserMentionIds
a949a9.evidence: Traced the mention pipeline: server-side `extractUserMentionIds` in pb_hooks/mention_notifications_lib.js scans `<span ...>` tags in comments.text/posts.content and regex-extracts the first `data-user-id` per tag, then creates a notification for each id (mention_notifications.pb.js fires on create/update). Modelled it in node against sanitized output: a user-controlled floating `data-user-id="X"` before the real attributes is preserved verbatim by the client sanitizer (which re-emits the FIRST `data-user-id` it finds) and parsed by the server regex, so a member could point a mention chip at a spoofed user id and trigger a notification to an arbitrary real user with forged mention copy. The impact is the same class of forged-notification spoofing already filed as vuln-0007 for the notifications collection, and the written evidence is a source+regex model rather than a live end-to-end replay (I did not fire it at a real user's inbox). Recording the gap rather than claiming it.

158ab9.risk_area: Field parsing / type-coercion bypass in the moderator-only manual user creation endpoint
158ab9.evidence: Implements manual player creation with a server-side `auth.getString('role') !== 'moderator'` gate (verified live: 403 for a plain user). Field parsing uses `asString()` which unwraps single-element arrays, and `rating_points` is coerced with `Number(...) || 0`. A potential goja type-coercion differential in the array/object branches could not be exercised because no moderator token was available for this engagement; the gate itself is present and correct on the paths tested.

84d5dc.risk_area: Confidentiality of other users' comments (cross-user read)
84d5dc.evidence: Comments are readable across users for any authenticated account (listRule `@request.auth.id != ""`), which allows enumerating other members' comment ids and content. Storing/updating remains ownership-scoped (PATCH and DELETE on a foreign comment both returned 404), and the read scope was explicitly treated as intended product behaviour rather than a finding. Noted so a later agent does not re-report cross-user comment reads as a confidentiality bug.

d12792.evidence: Anonymous request reaches the handler body with no auth gate: `GET /api/video-poster` with no Authorization header returns `400 {"error":"missing_params"}` (the handler's own validation ran) and `?collection=users&record=x&file=a.mp4` returns `404 {"error":"not_found"}`. Every sibling custom route returns 401 for the same anonymous call. Independently confirmed with byte-level retrieval of private member media in vuln-0001 (already filed by the SSTI/RCE & Injection Hunter agent); my own probes with a real gallery record id returned 404 because the gallery record has no video file stored. Recorded duplicate-free: report vuln-0001 covers this route; no second report filed.

d5652a.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization (privileged notification without role check)
d5652a.evidence: Confirmed live with the role=user token: the handler has no moderator-role check and trusts body.actorIsModerator. Order established by three probes: `{"event":"book","userIds":[me],"trainingId":"x","totalBookedCount":0}` (no actorId) -> `400 Missing required fields` (validation before authz); `actorId` = another user -> `403 Forbidden` (identity binding exists); `actorId`=self + nonexistent trainingId -> `404 Training not found`. So the authz check is absent, not merely ordered late. Already filed as vuln-0002 by the SSTI/RCE & Injection Hunter agent; no duplicate filed.

a9c105.surface: /api/stats/*  (growth, reach, reach/users, booking, trainings-count, growth/day, trainings-count/day, achievements, achievements/grants)
a9c105.evidence: Anonymous -> 401 `{"error":"Unauthorized"}` (no token at all). Role=user token -> 403 `{"error":"Forbidden"}`. `requireModerator(c)` at pb_hooks/statslib.js:835 checks `auth.getString('role') !== 'moderator'` and is called by all 9 stats routes in pb_hooks/stats.pb.js; every one re-tested live with the user token: growth, reach, reach/users, booking, trainings-count, growth/day, trainings-count/day, achievements, achievements/grants all returned 403.

6382f7.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization on account-merge primitives
6382f7.evidence: Anonymous -> 401, role=user -> 403 for all three: GET /api/users-claim-candidates, POST /api/users-claim-max, POST /api/users-unclaim-max. Source: pb_hooks/users_claim.pb.js lines 6-9 / 31-34 / 66-69, explicit `if (auth.getString('role') !== 'moderator') return c.json(403,...)` before body parsing and before claimlib.claimMax/unclaimMax.

ad8f50.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization (account destruction / account creation)
ad8f50.evidence: Anonymous -> 401, role=user -> 403, for POST /api/users-delete and POST /api/users-create-manual (tested with realistic bodies: `{"targetUserId":"zqath3none"}` and `{"full_name":"zqath3"}`). Gates at pb_hooks/users_delete.pb.js:7-14 and pb_hooks/users_manual.pb.js:7-14 run before userdeletelib.deleteUserAccount / manualuserlib.createManualUser.

aa605f.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization (admin backup / broadcast dispatch)
aa605f.evidence: Anonymous -> 401, role=user -> 403 for POST /api/admin-backup (body `{"type":"db"}`) and POST /api/admin-dispatch-now. POST /api/internal/backup-notify returns 403 to both anonymous and authenticated callers because it requires a one-shot X-Backup-Notify-Token consumed by backuplib.consumeNotifyToken (pb_hooks/backup.pb.js:46-58) — the auth header is irrelevant there, so it is not a BFLA surface at all.

0b7c57.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization on broadcast / template-mutation routes
0b7c57.evidence: Anonymous -> 401, role=user -> 403 for bot-notify-training-status, -edit, -create, -cancelled, -restored, even with realistic bodies containing a nonexistent trainingId and valid `changes` arrays — so the role check precedes all record lookup and every broadcastToAllUsers path. /api/max-bot-webhook -> 403 for both anonymous and authenticated callers unless the X-Max-Bot-Api-Secret header matches MAX_BOT_WEBHOOK_SECRET (bot_notifications.pb.js:397-406); tested with no header, "test", and "0". /api/bot-notify-membership-frozen and /api/notify-membership-topup -> 403 for both anonymous and user (membership_lifecycle.pb.js:25-27 / 42-45). /api/system-templates -> 403 anon and user; /api/system-templates-update -> 403 for both even with a valid-shaped `{"id":"zqath3x","title":"t"}` body, so the gate precedes the record lookup.

bbe1d2.evidence: GET /api/collections/_superusers/records -> 403 `{"message":"Only superusers can perform this action."}` for both anonymous and user tokens. GET /api/backups and GET /api/logs -> 401 anon / 403 user (superuser-only, PocketBase 0.23 gates these). GET /_/ -> nginx 401 with Basic-auth challenge (nginx/1.24.0). GET /api/settings -> 401 anon / 403 user. /api/collections/users/records/{id}/impersonate -> 404 (endpoint does not exist in this version). /api/collections/users/records/{id}/external-auths -> 404. No superuser material was reachable with a user token.

17b76f.surface: Route-shape bypasses on moderator-only custom routes (method override, trailing slash, case, encoded slash, doubled slash)
17b76f.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization via route shadowing / verb drift
17b76f.evidence: Tested method overrides, trailing slashes and case variants against a moderator-only route with the user token: X-HTTP-Method-Override: GET -> 404, trailing slash -> 404, GET /API/System-Templates -> 200 but body is the React SPA index.html (nginx static fallback, not the API handler — confirmed by the `<!DOCTYPE html><html lang="ru">` body). Every other verb/path-shape combination (PUT/PATCH/DELETE/POST on `/api/stats/growth`, `/api/stats/growth/`, `/api/Stats/Growth`, `/api/stats/growth%2f`, `/api/users-claim-candidates/`) returned PocketBase 404 "File not found"/"resource wasn't found", never a 200 from the guarded handler. `/api/stats//growth` returned 301 to the canonical path, which then enforces 403.

1daf51.surface: Custom-route moderator gate vs tampered JWT claims (collectionId confusion, injected role claim)
1daf51.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization via JWT claim trust (role / collectionId claims)
1daf51.evidence: Ten forged-token variants re-signed with the original (invalid) signature were rejected 401: `collectionId:""`, `collectionId` swapped to another collection id, `collectionId` omitted entirely, and an added `"role":"moderator"` claim. Decisive result: the forged token whose payload carries `role:"moderator"` still gets `401 Unauthorized` from `/api/stats/growth` and `/api/stats/achievements`, whereas the genuine token gets `403 Forbidden` — proving the server resolves `auth.getString('role')` from the users record and ignores any role claim carried in the JWT. The same forged token also fails record-scoped reads (404), so no privilege came from the tampered claims.

289c52.risk_area: SSRF / path traversal / arbitrary outbound fetch
289c52.evidence: Anonymous -> 401 for /api/yadisk-preview and /api/yadisk-content. With the user token, every non-Yandex destination was rejected client-side by the YADISK_URL_RE allowlist (yadisklib.js:7) before any outbound request: `http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/health`, `http://localhost/`, `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/`, `https://evil.example/d/x`, `file:///etc/passwd` all returned `400 {"error":"Некорректная ссылка Яндекс.Диска"}`. The suffix-confusion candidate `https://disk.yandex.ru.evil.example/d/x` was also rejected 400 (the regex anchors the host with no `/` allowed before `/d/`). Outbound fetches are built from the constant cloud-api.yandex.net host with the user URL only as an encoded `public_key` query parameter. `path` traversal (`../../../../etc/passwd`, `/../../etc/passwd`, `disk:/../../etc/passwd`) returned 404 from the Yandex metadata API, not a local file.

dcae5d.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization / unbounded resource consumption on the custom content-view writer
dcae5d.evidence: Anonymous -> 401. With the user token, `{"object_type":"x","object_id":"y"}` -> 400 `object_type must be post or tournament_post` and a valid-shaped `{"object_type":"post","object_id":"zqath3probe","source":"viewport"}` -> 200 `{"id":"pk094mpvi67cd8b","ok":true}`. The only write is one content_views row with `user` forced to the caller's own id (statslib.js createContentView sets `record.set('user', userId)` from auth), so this is a self-scoped analytics row, not a privileged action. No update/delete and no cross-user write. The row created during testing carries the `zqath3probe` marker object_id; content_views has no delete rule so it cannot be removed via the API.

34025a.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization / forged notification on a custom route
34025a.evidence: Anonymous -> 401; with the user token, a body naming a nonexistent comment id returns 404 `Comment not found`, i.e. the handler runs after the auth check and then requires the referenced comment's `author` to equal the caller (comment_replies.pb.js:56-58, `if (lib.getRelationId(reply,'author') !== String(auth.id)) return 403`). Also validated `{"collection":"comments","commentId":"zqath3none"}` -> 404, and a non-whitelisted collection is rejected 400 `Invalid payload` by the ALLOWED_COLLECTIONS check. The resulting notification is always addressed to the parent comment's author, so the caller cannot redirect it to an arbitrary recipient.

88be5f.evidence: Anonymous -> 401; with the user token `{"productIds":["fwlj07b87160284"]}` -> 200 `{"ok":true}`. The handler writes one audit_events row whose `subject` is derived server-side from `audit.actorInfo(auth)` with `source:'self'` (shop_audit.pb.js:148-190), so a user can only create an audit record attributed to themselves. Impact confirmed bounded: the caller cannot read it back — `GET /api/collections/audit_events/records` with the same user token returns 200 with `{"items":[],"totalItems":0}` because the rule is `@request.auth.role = "moderator"`. No privileged action, no cross-user effect, no data disclosure.

99008f.risk_area: Authentication bypass on the login route
99008f.evidence: `POST /api/max-auth` with a syntactically valid but unsigned initData (`auth_date=1&hash=deadbeef`) returns 401 `{"error":"invalid signature"}` for both anonymous and authenticated callers; the signature is recomputed with HMAC-SHA256 keyed by `$security.hs256(BOT_TOKEN,"WebAppData")` and compared with `$security.equal(signature, receivedHash)` (max-auth.pb.js:56-63), and `auth_date` must be within 300 s. Reachable and correctly rejecting forged input. Note: this route is the MAX Bridge login endpoint, so its exposure is intended. Broader max-auth signature-validation testing is owned by the Auth/JWT & max-auth Hunter agent.

e1a2db.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization across the whole custom routerAdd surface
e1a2db.evidence: Custom-route enumeration is complete: `grep -h routerAdd pb_hooks/*.pb.js` yields exactly 35 routes, and every one was exercised live against both an anonymous request and the role=user token (43 probes in the final matrix, plus earlier runs). Beyond the routes listed in the other coverage rows, /api/health (200 anon — PocketBase built-in liveness, no data) and /api/realtime (200 anon — SSE connect frame only, exposes a random clientId, no record subscription without a token) were the only remaining anonymous 200s. No undocumented custom route was found that grants a user token moderator capability. /api/settings is 401 anon / 403 user.

53ef31.evidence: `filter=author != @request.auth.id` returns 403 "Only superusers can filter by @request.". `fields=*,email` returns no additional field beyond what the list rule already permits. Filtering on a permitted field (max_id) only narrows the already-permitted list. No injection was demonstrated.
